newsitem.title: JAPAN: Iraq oil export unlikely this year-former official.
newsitem.headline: Iraq oil export unlikely this year-former official.

text.p: Iraqi oil is unlikely to be exported within this year as the United States is expected to try to further delay implementation of an oil-for-food deal, a former senior Iraqi oil official said in Tokyo on Thursday.
The United States is opposed to the partial oil-sales agreement between Iraq and the United Nations, as it would help Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, Chalabi said.
The United States may try to postpone the oil sales indefinitely, not only until after the presidential elections but also well beyond 1997, Chalabi said.
However, mounting pressure on the United States from France, Russia and other nations may pave the way for sales to start in January, he added.
At issue is a May 20 accord between Iraq and the United Nations that permits Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil.
